lead: Cerdà, chamfered corners and Modernisme: the Barcelona of regular blocks and stately buildings.
history: The Eixample was born in the mid-19th century, when Ildefons Cerdà designed the city's expansion beyond its walls: a grid of blocks with chamfered corners, wide streets and inner courtyards designed to bring in light and air. The bourgeoisie of the day filled it with Modernista buildings such as Casa Batlló and La Pedrera, and later came the Sagrada Família, which ended up as the symbol of Barcelona.

Its six neighbourhoods lie on either side of Carrer de Balmes, in the Dreta and the Esquerra, and each has its own character, from the elegance of Passeig de Gràcia to the market atmosphere of Sant Antoni. Anyone looking for a flat in the Eixample will usually find high ceilings, hydraulic tile floors, balconies and glazed galleries, and a daily life in which almost everything is a few steps away: shops, schools, transport and services.

Across its 6 neighbourhoods, the average sale price ranges from 4,603 €/m² in Sant Antoni to 6,224 €/m² in La Dreta de l'Eixample, and the average rent from 1,107 €/month in La Sagrada Família to 1,596 €/month in La Dreta de l'Eixample.

Here the floor, the orientation, whether the flat faces the street or the inside of the block, and the height and condition of the building and its owners' association all weigh heavily. That is why each property deserves a close look before you decide.
summary: The Eixample has 277,353 inhabitants in 7.46 km² and 6 neighbourhoods. It is the most populated district in Barcelona. Its average sale price was 5,323 €/m² in 2025, 25% above the city average. The average rent is 1,284 €/month.
